questions.question: Which committee recommended the formation of a new category of NBFC i.e., Non-Banking Financial Company-Micro Finance Institution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Malegam Committee.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• The creation of a separate category for NBFCs operating in the microfinance sector (NBFC-MFI) was done based on the recommendations of the Malegam Committee.
 
• The Malegam Committee was appointed by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) in 2010 to review the microfinance sector in India and provide recommendations for its growth and development.
 
• The committee recommended the creation of a separate category of NBFCs for microfinance to regulate and supervise them effectively, and to ensure that they comply with the prescribed norms and standards.
 
• The NBFC-MFIs are required to obtain a certificate of registration from the RBI and comply with the regulations on interest rates, lending practices, borrower protection, and reporting requirements.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• **Shah Committee:** This committee was appointed by the Reserve Bank of India in **1989** to review the working of the **monetary system in India** and to suggest measures for its improvement.
 
• **Kamath Committee:** This committee was appointed by the Reserve Bank of India in **2014 **to review the working of the **asset reconstruction companies** in India and to suggest measures for their improvement.

questions.question: Harrod Domar growth model is known for highlighting the role of savings and investments. Which Five-Year Plan in India was based on this model?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**First**.__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• First Five-Year Plan

 
 
• 1st five-year plan was from 1951 to 1956.
 
• The prime target of the first five-year plan of India was the** Development of agriculture**.
 
• The target Growth was 2.1 % and the Actual Growth was 3.6 %.
 
• It was based on Harrod-Domar.
 
• The influx of refugees, severe food shortage & mounting inflation confronted the country at the onset of the first five-year plan.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] Additional Information__Second Five Year Plan (1956-1961)

 
• The second five-year plan is based on the so-called Mahalanobis model.
 
• This was the USSR model Indianized by PC Mahalanobis, the founder of the Indian Statistical Institute and a close aide of Nehru.
 
• This model is known to have set the statistical foundations for state-directed investments and created the intellectual underpinnings of the license-raj through an elaborate input-output model.
 
• This Model suggested that there should be an emphasis on the heavy industries, which can lead the Indian Economy to a long-term higher growth path
 
• Started Industrial Policy Resolution 1956.

Third Five-Year Plan (1961-1966)

 
• The Third 5 year Plan focused on agriculture & enhancement in the production of wheat, but the succinct Sino - Indian War in the year 1962 exposed flaws in the economy & shifted the spotlight towards the Defence industry.
 
• On May 31 & June 1, 1961, the National Development Council considered the Draft Report on the Third Plan and generally approved it.
 
• In the course of this period, India's economy must not only enlarge swiftly but must, in unison, become independent and self-generating.
 
• This long-standing approach is projected to offer a wide-ranging design of expansion for the country's natural resources, industrial advance, and agricultural changes in the social structure & an incorporated scheme of regional & national development.

Fourth Five Year Plan (1969-1974)

 
• The fourth Five Year Plan was the first plan launched by the Indira Gandhi government amid the pressure of drought, devaluation, and inflationary recession.
 
• The country was fighting with population explosion, increased unemployment, poverty, and a shackling economy. In addition, the situation in East Pakistan (now independent Bangladesh) was becoming dire as the Indo-Pakistani War of 1971 and the Bangladesh Liberation War took place.
 
• Funds earmarked for industrial development had to be used for the war effort.
 
• The result was that this plan period was also no better than the third five-year plan.

questions.question: When did Dmitri Mendeleev invent the periodic table, ordering the symbols of the chemical elements according to their atomic weights?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1869**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Dmitri Mendeleev** invented the periodic table in **1869**, organizing elements based on their atomic weights and properties.
 
• Mendeleev left **gaps in the table** for elements yet to be discovered, predicting their properties accurately.
 
• On **March 6, 1869**, Mendeleev presented his first periodic table to the Russian Chemical Society.
 
• Mendeleev’s table demonstrated that when elements are arranged by increasing atomic weight, **certain chemical properties repeat periodically**.
 
• This periodic arrangement became the foundation for the modern periodic table used in chemistry today.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Periodic Law:** Mendeleev’s periodic table was based on the periodic law which states that **the properties of elements are a periodic function of their atomic weights**.
 
• **Modern Periodic Table:** Today, the periodic table is organized by **atomic number** (proton count) rather than atomic weight, as introduced by Henry Moseley in 1913.
 
• **Predicted Elements:** Mendeleev accurately predicted the existence and properties of elements like **germanium (eka-silicon)**, gallium (eka-aluminum), and scandium.
 
• **Contributors to Periodicity:** Other scientists like John Newlands (law of octaves) and Lothar Meyer worked on periodic classification, but Mendeleev’s table was more comprehensive and widely accepted.
 
• **Significance:** Mendeleev’s periodic table provided a systematic framework for studying chemical elements, aiding in the discovery of new elements and advancing the field of chemistry.

questions.question: Ethanoic acid is a synonym for which acidic liquid is used in kitchens around the world as a basic seasoning in the preparation and cooking of certain foods?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vinegar.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**Ethanoic acid:

__
 
• Ethanoic acid commonly known as acetic acid belongs to a group of carboxylic acids.
 
• Vinegar is dilute acetic acid. Vinegar used in our day to day life is a 5-8% solution of acetic acid (Ethanoic acid ) in water.
 
• It is extensively used in kitchens around the world as a basic seasoning and preservative in the preparation and cooking of certain foods.
 
• Its chemical formula is **CH3COOH.**
 
• Vinegar is made by the fermentation of ethanol, which is typically derived from wine, beer, or other alcoholic beverages. During fermentation, acetic acid bacteria convert the ethanol into acetic acid, which gives vinegar its sour taste and pungent odor.
 
• Vinegar is a versatile ingredient that can be used in a wide range of culinary applications, **such as salad dressings, marinades, sauces, pickles, and baked goods.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• Properties of Acetic Acid are as follows-

 
 
• Acetic acid has antibacterial qualities and hence used as an antiseptic.
 
• The manufacture of rayon fibre involves the use of ethanoic acid.
 
• It is useful in the treatment of cancer due to its direct injection into the tumour.
 
• Being the major constituent of vinegar, it finds use in the pickling of many vegetables.
 
• The manufacture of rubber involves the use of ethanoic acid.
 
• It is also used in the manufacture of various perfumes.
 
• It is widely used in the production of vinyl acetate monomer.

questions.question: Who among the following devised a policy that came to be known as the Doctrine of Lapse?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lord Dalhousie**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] __Key Points__ 

__
 
• The doctrine of Lapse:

 
 
• Lord Dalhousie introduced the Doctrine of Lapse for annexing the dependent states whose ruler died without a natural heir to succeed him.
 
• One kingdom after another was annexed simply by applying this doctrine:** Satara (1848), Sambalpur (1850), Udaipur (1852), Nagpur (1853) and Jhansi (1854).**
 
 
 
• Lord Dalhousie:
 
 
• In 1848, Lord Dalhousie arrived in India as the Governor-General and was determined to extend British rule over India.
 
• Dalhousie occupied the Punjab and Sindh through war and brought several subordinate states directly under the Company’s rule by annexing them on the basis of the Doctrine of Lapse. 
 
• Lord Dalhousie also introduced the Doctrine of Good of Governed under which Awadh (1856) and Punjab (1849) were annexed.
 
• Dalhousie established Public Works Department, the objective behind the formation of this department was the construction and maintenance of canals, roads, bridges, etc.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Lord Canning:

 
 
• Lord Canning served as Governor-General of India from 1856 to 1862.
 
• During his tenure, the Government of India Act, 1858 was passed which created the office of Viceroy to be held by the same person who was Governor-General of India.
 
• Thus, Lord Canning also served as the first Viceroy of India.
 
• The Mutiny of 1857, which he was able to suppress successfully,
 
• The Passing of the Indian Councils Act, 1861 which introduced a portfolio system in India,
 
• Bengal Rent Act (1859).
 
 

 
• Lord William Bentinck (1828-1835):

 
 
• Abolition of sati and other cruel rites (1829).
 
• Suppression of thugi (1830).
 
• Charter Act of 1833.
 
• Resolution of 1835, and educational reforms and introduction of English as the official language.
 
• Annexation of Mysore (1831), Coorg (1834) and Central Cachar (1834).
 
• Treaty of 'perpetual friendship with Ranjeet Singh.
 
• Abolished the provincial court of appeal and circuit.

questions.question: In which of the following cities is the Quwwat ul-Islam mosque situated?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Delhi.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• Quwwat-ul-Islam Mosque is situated in the Qutb complex in Delhi.
 
• It was built by Qutub-ud-din-Aibak in 1193 AD.
 
• The Quwwat-ul-Islam is best known for its tower of victory, celebrating the Muslim conquest of India.
 
• It is built of red sandstone, grey quartz, and white marble.
 
• It is an intricately designed structure built on the** principles of construction and ornamentation which was another feature of Islamic architecture**.
 
• Quwwat-ul Islam Mosque stands northeast of the __Qutb Minar.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Qutub-ud-din Aibak:

 
 
• ​He was the founder of the Slave dynasty.
 
• He assumed the title of 'Sultan' for the first time in the history of India.
 
• He made Lahore the capital and later Delhi.
 
• He was also known as 'Lakh Baksh' or giver of lakhs for his magnanimity, as he gave a lot of liberal donations. 
 
• He started the construction of the Qutub Minar in the memory of Khawaja Qutubuddin Bhaktiyar Kaki but could complete only the first storey. 
 
• Aibak is known for having commissioned the Qutb Minar in Delhi, and the Adhai Din Ka Jhopra in Ajmer.

questions.question: Which of the following schemes is available to people in the age group of 18 to 50 years and provides risk coverage of ₹2 lakh in case of death of the insured, due to any reason, at an annual premium of ₹436?

options.text: Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY)

questions.solution:

 __

• Aim - PMJJBY was launched to increase the reach of life insurance among citizens.

Maximum maturity age

 
 
 
Completion of 55 years (Age near Birthday)

1 year (renewable) – June 1 to May 31 each year

Premium

 
 
 
Rs. 436

 
 
 

 Premium payment mode
 Annual. However, the 1st-year premium depends on the quarter in which the scheme is opted for.

questions.question: 'Padhe Bharat’ reading campaign, launched by the Department of School Education and Literacy to support and encourage children to read for a joyful learning experience started on January 1, 2022, for a period of ________ days.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**100**____.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Union Education and Skill Development Minister Dharmendra Pradhan launched a 100-day Reading Campaign ‘Padhe Bharat’ on Jan 01, 2022. 
 
• Children studying in Balvatika to grade VIII will be part of this campaign.
 
• The reading campaign aims to have the participation of all stakeholders at the national and state levels including children, teachers, parents, community, educational administrators, etc.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

**Objectives of the Padhe Bharat Campaign **

 
• The campaign strives to support and motivate students, along with all stakeholders at the state and national levels, including schools, teachers, parents, and communities, to foster a joyful learning experience through reading.
 
• It has designed one activity per week per group,** emphasizing making reading an enjoyable activity and building a lifelong association with the joy of reading**.
 
• Children studying from **Balvatika to Grade 8** are the primary focus of the campaign.
 
• It also emphasizes Indian languages, including mother tongue/local/regional languages.
 
• The campaign celebrates International **Mother Tongue Day on 21st February** with the activity of **"Kahani Padho Apni Bhasa Main"** (Reading story in own language), promoting local languages and culture.
 
• The reading campaign will run from **1st January 2022 till 10th April 2022, spanning 100 days (14 weeks)**.
 
• The campaign aligns with the vision and goals of the foundational Literacy and Numeracy mission (NIPUN Bharat).

questions.question: 'Swachh Bharat Mission’ is associated with which public figure?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mahatma Gandhi.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• To accelerate the efforts to achieve universal sanitation coverage and to put the focus on sanitation, the Prime Minister of India launched the **Swachh Bharat Mission on 2nd October 2014.**
 
• Under the mission, all villages, Gram Panchayats, Districts, States and Union Territories in India declared themselves "open-defecation free" (ODF) by 2 October 2019 in First Phase.
 
• On the 150th birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi, by constructing over 100 million toilets in rural India.
 
• To ensure that the open defecation-free behaviours are sustained, no one is left behind, and that solid and liquid waste management facilities are accessible.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Jawaharlal Nehru

 
• Jawaharlal Nehru was the first Prime Minister of India.
 
• He was born on November 14, 1889, in Allahabad.
 
• November 14 is celebrated as Children's Day in India.
 
• He is the Prime Minister who has had the longest term in office.
 
• He served as the prime minister of India from 15th August 1947 to 1964.
 
• He is the architect of the Preamble of the Indian constitution.
 
• He was the Prime Minister of India during the Indo-China war in 1962.
 
• He served as the first chairman of the planning commission of India.
 
• He was honoured with the Bharat Ratna in 1955.
 
• The name Panchayati raj was given by Jawaharlal Nehru.
 
• National herald is the newspaper started by Jawaharlal Nehru.
 
• He is the first prime minister to die in harness.
 
• Glimpses of the world, Discovery of India are the famous works of Nehru.
 
• Shantivan is the cremation ground of Jawaharlal Nehru.
 
• He died on May 27, 1964, in New Delhi​​ 

Lal Bahadur Shastri

 
• He was born on 2nd October 1904 in Mughalsarai, a small railway town seven miles from Varanasi in Uttar Pradesh.
 
• Participated in the freedom movement since 1930.
 
• He joined the Kashi Vidyapeeth in Varanasi, one of the many national institutions set up in defiance of British rule.
 
• ‘Shastri’ was the bachelor’s degree awarded to him by the Vidya Peeth but has stuck in the minds of the people as part of his name.
 
• He was a minister in the Union Cabinet from 1951 to 1956 when he resigned taking responsibility for the railway accident and later from 1957-1964.
 
• He was India’s second Prime Minister (1964-66).
 
• He signed an agreement with then Ceylon (now Sri Lanka) on persons of Indian origin there, in 1964 — an endorsement of the importance of neighbourhood.
 
• He was the first person to be posthumously awarded the Bharat Ratna (1966).

Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel

 
• He was the first Deputy Prime Minister of India.
 
• He was often called Sardar.
 
• He was also called an Indian Bismarck.
 
• Served as the first Home Minister of India.
 
• He was appointed as the President of the Indian National Congress during the Karachi session in 1931.

questions.question: In December 2021, the ________ approved a $500 million loan to the Government of India to help improve the quality of the country’s school education and mitigate the impact of the Covid-19 pandemic on the students’ learning.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Asian Development Bank**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Asian Development Bank (ADB) approved a $500 million loan to the Government of India in December 2021 to help improve the quality of the country's school education and mitigate the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on the students' learning.
 
• The loan will be used to support India's flagship education program,** Samagra Shiksha Abhiyan**, which aims to improve the quality of school education across the country.
 
• The loan will also help in providing **additional support to students and teachers affected by the COVID-19 pandemic**, including the provision of digital devices and internet connectivity.
 
• ADB has been working closely with the Government of India to support its efforts in responding to the COVID-19 pandemic and **mitigating its impact on the country's economy and people**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** **Asian Development Bank**

 
• The Asian Development Bank is a regional development bank established on 19 December 1966.
 
• Which is headquartered in the Ortigas Center located in the city of Mandaluyong, Metro Manila, Philippines.
 
• The company also maintains 31 field offices around the world to promote social and economic development in Asia.
 
 
• Headquarters: Mandaluyong, Philippines
 
• Founded: 19 December 1966
 
• Motto: ADB is committed to achieving a prosperous, inclusive, resilient, and sustainable Asia & the Pacific while sustaining its efforts to eradicate extreme poverty.

questions.question: Till which year did the High Court of Delhi continue to exercise jurisdiction over Himachal Pradesh?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1971**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **In 1971, the state of Himachal Pradesh** was granted its own High Court, which replaced the jurisdiction of the High Court of Delhi in the state.
 
• The High Court of Delhi initially had jurisdiction over the **Union Territory of Delhi and the states of Himachal Pradesh and Punjab**.
 
• **In 1966**, Punjab was divided into two states - Punjab and Haryana - and the jurisdiction of the High Court of Delhi was limited to the Union Territory of Delhi and Himachal Pradesh.
 
• The state of Himachal Pradesh was granted its own High Court on January 25, 1971, by the Himachal Pradesh High Court Act, 1971.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The highest judicial court in a state is the High Court.
 
• It is termed as the second-highest in the country after the Supreme Court of India.
 
• The Parliament passed the Indian High Courts Act 1861 which suggested the establishment of High Courts in three Presidencies: Calcutta, Madras, and Bombay.

questions.question: Which ecologist is famous for studying plant life in the Indiana Dunes in 1896?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Henry Chandler Cowles__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

 
• Henry Chandler Cowles studied ecological succession in the Indiana Dunes of Northwest Indiana in the 1890s.
 
• Henry Chandler Cowles (1869-1939) was a University of Chicago botany professor and conservationist, his studies of plant life in the Indiana Dunes made Cowles one of America's most notable early ecologists.
 
• In 1896, Cowles traveled to the southern shore of Lake Michigan to see the Indiana Dunes for the first time and studied them.
 
• His study explained the development and distribution of local plant communities in terms of topography, moisture, wind, erosion, sedimentation, and other geological processes.

questions.question: The layer of earth that separates the crust from the core is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mantle.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

The mantle: 

__
 
• The mantle extends up to a depth of 2900 km below the crust.
 
• It **separates the crust from the core**.
 
• The upper part of the mantle is known as the asthenosphere.
 
• Nearly 84% of the earth’s volume and 67% of the earth’s mass is occupied by the mantle.
 
• The major constituent elements of the mantle are Silicon and Magnesium and hence it is also termed as SIMA.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**The crust:

 
• The crust is the uppermost layer over the earth’s surface.
 
• It is the thinnest layer.
 
• it is only about 5 km on the ocean floors, which mainly consists of silica and alumina thus called sial (si-silica and al-alumina), and 35 km on the continental masses, which mainly consists of silica and alumina.

The core:

 
• The innermost layer is the core with a radius of about 3500 km and divided into Inner and Outer core.
 
• It is called nife (ni – nickel and fe – ferrous – iron) as it's mainly made up of nickel and iron.
 
• Central core is called the Inner core and has a very high temperature and pressure.

questions.question: Iron age is so named because during this time iron mostly replaced _________ in implements and weapons, beginning in the Middle East and South-eastern Europe.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**bronze**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Iron Age is a period in human history characterized by the widespread use of iron tools and weapons.
 
• This period began around **1200 BCE in the Middle East **and gradually spread to other parts of the world.
 
• Before the Iron Age, bronze was the preferred material for making tools and weapons.
 
• **Bronze is an alloy made from copper and tin.​**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• The most significant development was the use of** iron for tools, weapons, and agricultural implements**.
 
• Iron is stronger and more durable than bronze, the dominant material of the preceding era.
 
• Iron led to advancements in **agriculture, construction, and warfare**. For example, iron plowshares improved farming efficiency, while iron weapons gave rise to powerful warrior classes.
 
• The Iron Age saw the transition from **small tribal settlements to larger, more complex societies**. This was likely facilitated by increased **agricultural productivity and trade enabled by iron tools**.
 
• The Painted Grey Ware culture, associated with the early Iron Age, is characterized by distinctive pottery and iron tools found across North India.
 
• In the later period, we witnessed the** rise of powerful Mahajanapadas**, competing states that laid the foundation for larger empires like **the Mauryas and Guptas**.

questions.question: Which country celebrates one of the famous festivals known as Paro Tschechu?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bhutan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Paro Tschechu** is a famous annual religious festival celebrated in **Bhutan**.
 
• It is a four-day festival held in the Paro Valley of Bhutan, usually in **March or April**, to commemorate the birth anniversary of** Guru Rinpoche, the patron saint of Bhutan**.
 
• The festival features colorful traditional **dances, mask performances, and religious rituals performed by monks** and laypeople in elaborate costumes and masks.
 
• The festival also attracts a large number of tourists from around the world who come to witness the vibrant cultural heritage of Bhutan.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

 
• **Japan** is known for its own unique festivals such as the **Cherry Blossom Festival and the Gion Matsuri Festival**.
 
• **Thailand **is known for festivals such as **Songkran (Thai New Year) and Loi Krathong (Festival of Lights)**.
 
• **Burma **is known for festivals such as **Thingyan (Burmese New Year) and Taunggyi Tazaungdaing (Hot Air Balloon Festival)**.
